hero.title: Forward Deployed Engineer Roadmap
hero.subtitle: This roadmap establishes Python and AI engineering fundamentals along with FDE SDLC. From Stage 3,we will be learning to build an unified customer engagement—instructor-guided Todo labs and independent deliverables on the Customer support ticketing system scenario.

phases.label: Section 1 · 15 h
phases.detail: Stages 1–2: Software engineering and AI engineering fundamentals

phases.label: Section 2 · 15 h
phases.detail: Stages 3–9: BRD, UI/UX, architecture, backend, frontend, deployment, Langfuse/evals/obs/guardrails

phases.label: Section 3 · 10 h
phases.detail: Stage 10: One e-commerce Fullstack Agentic RAG capstone

capabilities: Write reliable Python that calls APIs, validates data with Pydantic and ships as a tested FastAPI service
Prompt, evaluate, and connect LLMs with structured output, tools, RAG, and LangGraph agents
Run structured customer discovery and author a crisp one-page business requirements document (BRD)
Define user flows, wireframes, reference architecture, role-based access, and latency/cost trade-offs
Develop, test, and harden customer solutions locally with a 20-question regression set
Deploy to Render or AWS with secrets in env, Langfuse traces/evals, and incident runbooks
Complete IT security questionnaires, run sponsor readouts, and deliver production handover packages
Deliver one integrated e-commerce capstone: full-stack commerce, multi-agent store assistant, and agentic RAG in a single application

faq.question: How long does this roadmap take?
faq.answer: 40 hours total: Section 1 (Foundations, 15h — 3h software engineering + 12h AI engineering), Section 2 (FDE SDLC, 15h), and Section 3 (single e-commerce capstone, 10h). Move on when you meet each stage’s "ready to move on" checkpoint.

faq.question: What does the roadmap cover?
faq.answer: Ten stages: Python and AI foundations (Stages 1–2), FDE SDLC and delivery (Stages 3–9: BRD, UI/UX, architecture, backend and frontend development, deployment, Langfuse/evals/observability/guardrails), and one integrated e-commerce capstone (Stage 10). Stages 3–9 use one customer story—Customer support ticketing system—while tutored labs use a smaller Todo app so beginners can practice safely before working on Customer support ticketing system alone.

faq.question: Why Todo in labs and Customer support ticketing system in assignments?
faq.answer: Stages 1–2 are concept labs only (no customer storyline). From Stage 3 onward, tutored labs use the Todo app and assignments use the Customer support ticketing system retail scenario.

faq.question: What will I be able to do after?
faq.answer: Stand up tested APIs and RAG prototypes, run customer discovery, produce BRDs and architecture diagrams, develop and test solutions, deploy to Render or AWS, configure Langfuse observability, pass enterprise security reviews, and build multi-agent applications.

faq.question: How are the 40 hours split?
faq.answer: Section 1 is 15 hours (Stage 1: 3h — FDE Intro, Python/FastAPI reads, Git and cloud last; Stage 2: 12h AI — LLM, RAG, agents, MCP and guardrails). Section 2 is 15 hours: BRD 1h, UI/UX 1h, architecture 1.5h, development backend 4h, development frontend 3h, deployment 3h, Langfuse/evals/observability/guardrails and handover 1.5h. Section 3 is 10 hours — one e-commerce Fullstack Agentic RAG capstone in four modules.

faq.question: What is the capstone in Section 3?
faq.answer: One integrated e-commerce application (10h total): four modules—full-stack commerce (React + FastAPI + PostgreSQL), multi-agent store assistant (LangGraph), agentic RAG over product manuals (ChromaDB), and deployment plus demo.

faq.question: Is progress saved? Do I need an account?
faq.answer: Progress is saved in your browser (localStorage). No login or backend is required for the FDE roadmap.

capstone.title: Section 3: Capstone (10h)
capstone.intro: One e-commerce Fullstack Agentic RAG application in four modules: full-stack commerce, multi-agent store assistant, agentic product-manual RAG with ChromaDB, then deployment and demo. Each module covers what you will do and what you will learn.
deliverables: Module 1: Full-stack commerce foundation — React, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, customer journey
Module 2: Multi-agent store assistant — LangGraph orchestrator and specialist agents
Module 3: Agentic RAG — product manuals, ChromaDB, cited answers, refusal behavior
Module 4: Deployment and demo — repeatable run, POC URL, smoke tests, handover narrative

strongWork.title: Full-stack commerce verified first
strongWork.body: Browse, cart, checkout, and order persistence in PostgreSQL are tested before AI layers are added.

strongWork.title: Clear agent responsibilities
strongWork.body: LangGraph orchestrator routes to specialist agents with scoped database tool permissions and clear boundaries.

strongWork.title: Grounded RAG retrieval
strongWork.body: ChromaDB retrieval over approved manuals provides citations and explicit "I don’t know" refusal behavior without cart mutations.

strongWork.title: Single unified interface
strongWork.body: One React client and FastAPI service cleanly separating store actions and product manual assistance modes.

stages.name: Software Engineering (Python)
stages.cardBlurb: FDE Intro (role and Antigravity), then Python/FastAPI reads—Git and cloud last—plus hands-on labs.
stages.description: Understand how the FDE course flows, then build reliable Python and a small FastAPI API with validation and tests.
outcomes: Explain the FDE role and SDLC stages used in this course
Write Python that handles files, JSON, and API calls safely
Validate request and response data with Pydantic
Ship a minimal tested FastAPI service
stages.readyWhen: You can explain the course flow and stand up a tested FastAPI API with /health and one resource in a day.

reads.title: FDE role, SDLC lifecycle, and how this course is structured
